questions.q: During a match, a footballer notices an unmarked teammate and quickly selects an appropriate pass. Which component of mental fitness is most directly involved?
options: Cognitive functioning.
Social exclusion.
Structural access.
Physical strength.
questions.feedback: Cognitive functioning supports information processing, decision-making and problem-solving during performance.

questions.q: Which statement best describes directive coaching?
options: The coach provides clear instructions and demonstrations and makes most immediate decisions.
The athletes independently design the session without coach input.
The coach avoids correcting unsafe technique.
The athletes determine all safety procedures.
questions.feedback: Directive coaching is coach-led and can be useful when clear instruction, demonstrations or immediate safety guidance are required.

questions.q: Why is the Social-Ecological Model useful when examining physical activity behaviour?
options: It assumes one factor usually explains behaviour completely.
It focuses only on personal motivation.
It recognises that several interacting factors can influence behaviour.
It removes the need to consider barriers and enablers.
questions.feedback: The model recognises that physical activity and sedentary behaviour are shaped by multiple interacting influences.

questions.q: Why is increased research involving female athletes important for physical-activity prescription?
options: It allows one training program to be prescribed for all female athletes.
It proves menstrual-cycle phase is the main influence on sporting performance.
It can improve evidence used to develop more individualised exercise programs.
It removes the need to consider an athlete's symptoms and training responses.
questions.feedback: Better research can improve understanding of individual responses and support more informed physical-activity prescription.

questions.q: A survey finds that 72% of urban adolescents can reach organised sport within 20 minutes, compared with 38% of adolescents in remote communities. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Remote adolescents are less motivated to participate.
Urban adolescents have no barriers to sport participation.
Travel and service availability may create greater access barriers for remote adolescents.
Geographic location alone determines participation because travel time controls access for adolescents.
questions.feedback: The data suggest a difference in geographic access, but they do not prove differences in motivation or show that geography is the only influence.

questions.kk: Benefits of Regular Participation in Movement
questions.q: Which benefit is most closely associated with social health and wellbeing?
options: Developing communication and teamwork skills
Reducing the risk of type 2 diabetes
Improving the ability to process information
Developing a stronger sense of personal meaning
questions.feedback: Communication and teamwork help people interact effectively and build meaningful relationships, supporting social health and wellbeing.

questions.q: Which action best demonstrates a sporting club taking responsibility for safe coaching?
options: Providing codes of conduct, coach education, supervision and clear reporting pathways
Assuming a screening check guarantees safe behaviour and therefore removing the need for supervision, training or reporting procedures
Leaving each coach to create their own safeguarding rules
Responding only after serious harm occurs
questions.feedback: Safe coaching environments require organisational systems such as recruitment checks, education, supervision, codes of conduct and accessible reporting.

questions.kk: Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines
questions.q: Why are functional activities particularly relevant within the older-adult guidelines?
options: They are the only physical activity older adults are permitted to complete under the guidelines
They replace the need for muscle-strengthening activity.
They target mobility, balance and coordination, which can support physical function and reduce falls risk.
They must always be completed at vigorous intensity.
questions.feedback: Functional activities target mobility, balance and coordination and are especially relevant to maintaining function and reducing falls risk.

questions.kk: Prevalence and Trends of Physical Activity, Physical Inactivity and Sedentary Behaviour
questions.q: Data: children aged 2–5 — 39% did not meet the physical activity component; 75% did not meet the screen-time component; 83% did not meet both. What stands out most clearly?
options: Physical activity non-compliance was nearly twice screen-time non-compliance.
Screen-time non-compliance was particularly high and combined compliance was low.
Most children met both components.
Screen time was not a meaningful issue for this age group.
questions.feedback: Three quarters did not meet the screen-time component and 83% did not meet both components, showing substantial non-compliance.

questions.q: A 22-year-old runner has a high proportion of slow-twitch fibres and regularly completes endurance training. Which factor most directly supports their aerobic power according to the fitness-component factors studied?
options: High joint stability because a more stable joint always increases oxygen delivery and therefore directly raises aerobic energy production
Large adipose stores
A greater proportion of slow-twitch fibres
A faster muscle contraction speed
questions.feedback: A greater proportion of slow-twitch fibres supports aerobic metabolism and is a factor associated with higher aerobic power.
